step1_analysis.circuit_type: Passive RC network (BJT small-signal parasitic model)
step1_analysis.description: A passive RC network representing the parasitic capacitances and resistances of a bipolar junction transistor. It is used in the paper for open-circuit time constant (OCTC) delay analysis of high-speed CML latches and frequency dividers.

paper_reference.title: Design Analysis and Circuit Enhancements for High-Speed Bipolar Flip-Flops

Operating_Frequency_Support.description: Maximum frequency supported by the RC time constant of the parasitic network.

sky130_expected.calculation: Bandwidth ~ 1 / (2 * pi * sum(R_i * C_i)). With typical values, tau ~ 1.1ps, yielding ~144 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The passive network's time constant must be small enough to not bottleneck the 96 GHz operation reported in the paper.

DC_Power.description: DC power dissipated by the biasing and parasitic resistors.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on assumed typical parasitic and load resistor values for a high-speed CML stage.

High_Freq_Gain.description: AC coupling gain from Base to Collector at high frequencies.

sky130_expected.reasoning: At high frequencies, capacitors act as shorts, and the gain is determined by the resistor divider.

Peak_Transient_Voltage.description: Peak voltage at the Collector during a step input at the Base.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The step input couples through the capacitors, adding to the DC bias voltage.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, high-frequency AC gain, and transient step response of the BJT parasitic RC network.
